background.summary: The conversation began by evaluating a proposed repeated diet of two double-carnitas Chipotle bowls, 40 g dark chocolate, two bananas, water and supplements. This is a scenario, not a confirmed eaten day.
Planned yogurt, almonds, berries and mango alongside revised Chipotle bowls; proposed changes to supplements and iodized salt. Plans and dose discussions are not recorded as actual intake.

Reported cutting chocolate, replacing fish oil with sardines and developing a Trader Joe's plus RT chicken alternative. Vitamin D was the only supplement described in the pattern, but no actual daily dose was confirmed.

Desk work with brief interval sessions and gym visits. Track and gym were described as two out of every three days, reached by scooter; sauna was planned but not started in this description. This activity description does not establish maintenance calories.

Planned raspberries, orange, tomato, two kiwis, one red pepper, two bananas, low-fat yogurt, walnuts, low-sodium small oily fish, broth and vitamin D. The next actual report had four bananas and no kiwis, broth or vitamin D; the plan must not fill those missing foods.

Reported diluting yogurt into ayran and drinking it across the day. Water dilution adds no yogurt nutrients, while any added salt remains unmeasured. Preferred bottled broth over collagen powder; had 200 mg caffeine capsules, with no daily ingestion recorded.

While returning to heavier training, reported about a week of progressively uncomfortable pain at the front of the left shoulder and backing off exercises that loaded it. This is a self-report, without a diagnosis or measured severity.
Decided to remove ordinary chicken broth from future shopping after reporting that it was not enjoyed. No replacement was required; earlier actual broth consumption remains in its dated record.

Wants whole fruit that can be bought and finished; dislikes precut fruit and mangos, pineapple is too large. Pomegranate arils are an acceptable exception. Can eat more green kiwis. Likes the navel orange; prefers one red bell pepper. These preferences guide future shopping rather than adding foods to an eaten-day log.
